data_output.description: data.load(data_dir, max_rows_per_split=None) must return the existing split mapping for train, valid, and test, with rows retained in canonical source-file iteration order after the existing date filtering and optional prefix truncation. Each internal row must retain date, user_id, video_id, tab, canonical hour, canonical weekday, and label information sufficient for encode(). data.encode(splits) must return (encoded, dimension), where encoded[name] is exactly (features, labels, users). features is an np.int32 array of shape (N, 5), with columns in exact order user_id, video_id, tab, hour, weekday. Each cell is a globally offset categorical index. Each field vocabulary is built only from training rows and has its own unknown index for absent non-training values. labels remains an np.float32 vector derived only from long_view, users remains the user_id vector used for grouping, and dimension equals the total count of all five vocabulary dimensions including unknown buckets.

model_input.description: Model receives the encoded np.int32 feature matrix with five globally offset categorical indices per row in exact column order [user_id, video_id, tab, hour, weekday]. It must continue to add one learned scalar weight for each feature index plus its scalar bias; no interaction or model architecture change is part of this experiment. The fixed trainer must continue to train on encoded["train"] and save predictions_valid.npz containing exactly row_ids and scores, with row_ids equal to np.arange(validation_row_count, dtype=np.int64) and scores aligned one-for-one to canonical validation row order.

feature_engineer.objective: Extend the additive ID feature matrix with exactly the request-context categorical fields tab, hour, and weekday, using only eligible raw log fields and the schema's canonical derivations.
required_changes: Change FIELDS from ["user_id", "video_id"] to ["user_id", "video_id", "tab", "hour", "weekday"], preserving this exact field order so the existing ID fields remain first.

While reading each log row in load(), retain raw tab and hourmin in addition to date, user_id, video_id, and the long_view label. Use the exact raw column names row["tab"] and row["hourmin"]; do not introduce aliases or read any other source columns.
Derive hour exactly as integer floor(numeric hourmin / 100), i.e. int(float(row["hourmin"]) // 100), and validate that the result is in 0..23; raise ValueError for an out-of-range value.

Derive weekday exactly from the YYYYMMDD date using calendar weekday semantics with Monday=0 through Sunday=6, e.g. datetime.datetime.strptime(str(date_value), "%Y%m%d").weekday(). Import datetime as needed.
Store tab, derived hour, and derived weekday in each internal row tuple so encode() can extract them without rereading files.
Update encode() raw(row) to return exactly [user_id, video_id, tab, hour, weekday] from the expanded row tuple.

Fit one categorical vocabulary per all five FIELDS exclusively from splits["train"]. For every non-training split, map values absent from that field's train vocabulary to that field's dedicated unknown bucket exactly as the current implementation does.

Retain the current per-field contiguous offset construction and return signature: encoded is a mapping of split name to (features, labels, users), and dimension is the sum of all field vocabulary sizes including unknown buckets.
Ensure features has dtype np.int32 and shape (number_of_rows_in_split, 5); labels and users retain their current meanings and dtypes.
preserve: Do not modify model.py, train.py, or config.json.

Keep the model-facing representation as one globally offset categorical index per field per row; no interactions, feature crosses, dense numeric features, target encodings, aggregates, joins, or additional feature families may be added.
Keep the existing files and split boundaries: training is 20220408 through 20220421, validation is 20220422 through 20220428, and test is 20220429 through 20220508.
Use only user_id, video_id, tab, hourmin, date, and long_view from the standard log files. long_view remains label-only and must not enter raw(row) or features.

Preserve source-row iteration order within each input file and preserve the resulting selected-row order for every split; do not sort, shuffle, deduplicate, or filter rows beyond existing date selection and optional max_rows_per_split truncation.
Preserve the existing train-only vocabulary behavior, unknown handling, label creation, and users output used by trainer.py's proxy metric.

Do not use forbidden, excluded, or quarantined fields, including time_ms, outcome fields other than label construction from long_view, statistical snapshots, user-feature files, or video-feature files.
coordination_notes: The existing Model accepts any number of offset categorical columns and sums their weights, so no model.py change is required. The output feature matrix must remain suitable for Model.logits(features), Model.step(features, labels), and Model.predict(features).
trainer.py and config.json remain unchanged: optimizer, loss, epochs, batching, patience, learning rate, l2, seed, and split are fixed by the parent configuration.

The fixed training command relies on encoded["valid"] retaining canonical validation source-row order. Its existing np.savez output must therefore continue to contain row_ids=np.arange(len(valid_labels), dtype=np.int64) and one score per validation row in exactly that order.
The contract-check path truncates each split to at most 64 rows before encoding. The expanded five-column feature matrix must work unchanged under that path and produce finite predictions.
The required ablation is exactly the three added categorical fields tab, hour, and weekday; do not add user-by-context, video-by-context, or any other interaction parameterization.

reasoning: The requested ablation changes only the input categorical feature family. The current additive model is column-count agnostic and the current trainer already preserves validation order and emits the required row_ids and scores archive, so activating only feature_engineer is sufficient and avoids unnecessary architecture or training changes. tab is an eligible raw log field; hour and weekday are derived solely with the canonical hourmin and date recipes. All five categorical vocabularies will be fit on the training split only, with validation/test unseen values assigned to field-specific unknown buckets.
